title: Search response
description: The 200 body of GET /wp-json/resource-hub/v1/search?q=…&page=n, the plugin's search route: one page of the published resources and pages that match q, at a fixed 12 per page. q is trimmed and its whitespace runs collapsed to one space, and must then be 2 to 100 characters; page is 1 to 10 and defaults to 1. Anything else is answered with a WordPress REST error (wp-error.schema.json). The body lists IDs and kinds only, by design: the front end then reads the objects with GET /wp-json/wp/v2/resources?include={ids}&orderby=include&_embed and GET /wp-json/wp/v2/pages?include={ids}&orderby=include, so one code path renders a resource everywhere and this route stays small and cacheable.

items.description: This page's matches in the search engine's order, resources and pages mixed. At most 12, the page size. Empty when nothing matches, and for a page past the last one.

total.description: How many published resources and pages match q in all, as the search engine counts them. Not capped: it can exceed what the 10 reachable pages hold, so a front end can say there are more results than it can show. 0 when nothing matches.

pages.description: How many pages of results can be asked for: total divided by 12 and rounded up, capped at 10, the largest page the route accepts. 0 when total is 0. Matches past the tenth page are counted in total and never listed.

item.description: One match: its post ID and which kind of content it is, which says which core collection to read it from.

id.description: The post ID of the match, to pass to its collection's include parameter.

type.description: The match's post type: resource for a resource, read from /wp/v2/resources; page for a WordPress page the front end serves at its path, read from /wp/v2/pages.
